top.description: LaNorris Sellers (left) of the South Carolina Gamecocks drops back to pass in the first half Nov. 7, 2026 against the Texas A&M Aggies at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia, South Carolina. (Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) Take a look at the box score of the 17-9 road loss for Texas A&M football to No. 21 South Carolina and you'd be forgiven for being a little perplexed. On paper, the Aggies performed well. They put up 457 yards to the Gamecocks 360, rushed for 206 yards to the hosts' 109, possessed the ball for almost 10 more minutes and - for just the second time this season against a Power Four opponent - did not turn the ball over. David Olano of the Texas A&M Aggies kicks a field goal in the first half Nov. 7, 2026 against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Williams-Brice Stadium in Columbia, South Carolina. (Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) Yet in what has become a familiar pattern this year, A&M was unable to score a single touchdown, putting up just nine points as the Aggies fell to 4-5 on the year and just 1-5 in Southeastern Conference play. A&M is the first team in NCAA history to have more than 450 total yards of offense, zero turnovers, and score zero touchdowns in the same game, according to TexAgs. "(We) gave a lot of stuff away," head coach Mike Elko said. "You can't get down there as much as we did and not come away with points when you're playing a team like that. … But at the end of the day, we had a chance to win a game in the fourth quarter, and we didn't do it." Success on the ground Running back Reubem Owens II entered this season as the Aggies' RB1, but had fallen down the depth chart as the year went on behind freshman KJ Edwards and sophomore Jamarion Morrow. But with Edwards recovering from the flu and Morrow - who recorded just one carry - banged up, according to Elko, Owens seemed to play as if he wanted to regain that RB1 title. On the Aggies' first play from scrimmage, Owens scampered 40 yards downfield to give A&M an explosive start to the day. "I just had a good week," Owens said. " … I felt it before the game that it was going to be one of the ones. Coach gave me the opportunity and my O-line gave me the opportunity, and I put it out there." By halftime, Owens led the Aggies with 64 yards on 10 carries as the Aggies picked up 101 yards on the ground - a number made even more impressive by A&M's defense, which held South Carolina to just 36 rushing yards in the first half. "We challenged them to be physical," Elko said. "I thought that was going to be a big part of that game. They're a really good run offense, they're a really good run defense. In this environment, we knew we were going to have to control the run game. They got great edge rushers, and again, we did what we wanted to do to the red area, and in the red area we just couldn't finish." top.description: Fans celebrate goal against their own team in Série B 🇧🇷 Náutico fans were at the center of an unusual scene during the team's match against CRB this Saturday (7), in the penultimate round of Série B. The game took place at Aflitos stadium, home of Timbu, but the home fans celebrated the goals scored by...the opposition! The reason is the local rivalry: Sport are competing directly with CRB for promotion to the first division. With Náutico no longer having anything to play for in the league, the fans celebrated a result that hurt their rivals, as CRB won 3–0. And it wasn't just the fans who showed little interest in Saturday's game. On Thursday (5), Náutico's board decided to send nine players, including regular starters, on holiday early. The situation sparked criticism beyond the rivalry in Pernambuco. Atlético-GO, who are also competing with CRB for promotion, released a statement on social media saying they had "never taken the field to lose, because that's dirty play." The statement does not mention Náutico, but stresses that "the Brazilian Série B Championship is one of the most fiercely contested competitions in the world and must be respected by all 20 clubs until the very end." top.title: Justin Gaethje’s manager shuts down Ilia Topuria rematch: ‘Will never happen!’
top.description: WASHINGTON, DC - MAY 06: (L-R) Ilia Topuria and Justin Gaethje face off on the South Lawn in front of the White House on May 06, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Zuffa LLC) The fans want a Justin Gaethje vs. Ilia Topuria rematch. Ilia Topuria wants it. The UFC wants it. But Justin Gaethje does not, according to his manager Ali Abdelaziz. Gaethje took the UFC lightweight title off Topuria in a brutal war on the White House lawn back in June, forcing Topuria’s corner to throw in the towel after the fourth round. Few had given Justin a chance of winning, and now “The Highlight” seems uninterested in giving Ilia a chance to win that fight back. Topuria just did a media blitz of interviews, and a big topic of discussion was a potential Gaethje rematch. Topuria put up a poll on social media to ask his fans who they’d rather see him face off against. After 24 hours, Justin Gaethje edged out Paddy Pimblett, 474,000 votes to 385,000. Alas, there continues to be no interest in the fight from Gaethje’s side. 🚨‼️Ali Abdelaziz completely shuts down the possibility of an Ilia Topuria rematch 👀 🗣️“This rematch will never happen, and I agree with him. His brother saved his life. It's very hard to come back from the trauma of a fight like that. I've seen Justin do this to many people,… pic.twitter.com/WxwASLAyfQ — FightLuck (@FightluckBet) November 8, 2026 “This rematch will never happen,” Gaethje’s manager Ali Abdelaziz tweeted and later deleted. Abdelaziz also referred to a quote from Topuria thanking his brother for stopping the fight after the fourth round. “I agree with him – his brother saved his life,” Abdelaziz wrote. “It’s very hard to come back from the trauma of a fight like that. I’ve seen Justin do this to many people, and coming back wasn’t easy for them. Wishing him the best of luck.” Gaethje continues to flirt with retirement and has said he won’t come back unless it’s for a massive fight. And while the Topuria rematch certainly qualifies, it’s also a fight he won in dominant fashion. There’s no way for him to improve on the performance he gave on the White House lawn against Topuria, so why go back and do it again immediately? ‘Because it’d be awesome,’ is the obvious answer. But Gaethje is looking to wrap his career up on his terms, not be the foil in Ilia Topuria’s comeback story. If Abdelaziz is giving us a legit look into Gaethje’s mindset and not just posturing as a negotiation tactic, we’ll have to resign ourselves to … Gaethje vs. Tsarukyan or Volkanovski? Not the worst consolation prizes.

top.title: Georgia Crushes Ole Miss While Ohio State Crashes Out
top.description: Nov 7, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Georgia Bulldogs defensive back KJ Bolden (4) and defensive back Demello Jones (8) react during the first half against the Mississippi Rebels at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Georgia football obliterated Ole Miss 42-7 on Saturday to end a 16-game home winning streak for the Rebels. The Bulldogs rolled past their SEC rivals in Oxford and put themselves back in the hunt for the number one spot. This win comes right after No. 1 Miami lost to Notre Dame, clearing the path for Georgia to climb back to the top of the US LBM Coaches Poll. Quarterback Gunner Stockton looked sharp even though he threw the ball fewer times than usual. He completed nine of 15 passes for 186 yards and tossed four touchdowns against the Rebels. Wide receiver Talyn Taylor caught three of those scores, including a massive 58-yard strike that sparked the rout. The running game was just as deadly, with Nate Frazier gaining 107 yards on 16 carries to wear down the Ole Miss defense. Georgia’s defense held star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss to just 170 passing yards with no touchdowns and one interception. Ohio State’s Playoff Hopes Fade While Georgia soared, Ohio State hit the floor hard with a home loss to Oregon. The Buckeyes now have two straight defeats, and their chances for the College Football Playoff look like they are toast. Per Yahoo Sports, the AP voters will drop Ohio State in the rankings after the Buckeyes were handled at home by Oregon. This follows a previous loss to USC, leaving Ryan Day’s team with a shaky resume despite wins against Iowa and Indiana. The collapse of Ohio State highlights how fast things can change in college football. Teams that look strong in September can crater by November if they lose key games. The Buckeyes are now in a spot where they need to win out just to stay relevant. Meanwhile, Georgia used their own loss to Auburn as a reset to become the most complete team in the country. They have turned back into a dominant force when it matters most. The New Order at the Top With Miami’s loss and Georgia’s win, the top of the polls is set for a major shakeup. Following their Holy War victory over BYU, Utah holds a perfect 9-0 record, marking the first top-10 clash in the series history. The Utes are now one of the last two unbeaten teams left in the nation and are locked in for the Big 12 title game. Per Yahoo Sports, Utah could rise to No. 2 in the coaches poll while UCLA moves to No. 3 after staying perfect. Notre Dame also secured its spot in the playoff chase by beating Miami 31-24 in South Bend. By executing a critical red zone stop with less than four minutes remaining, the Fighting Irish prevented a devastating defeat. They now look forward to Boston College, SMU, and Syracuse to end the year.

top.description: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - NOVEMBER 01: Michael Taaffe #16 of the Miami Dolphins celebrates during the first half of the game against the New England Patriots at Hard Rock Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins lost to the New England Patriots last weekend, dropping to 1-6 and reminding everyone this is a rebuilding year. They held a 13-3 halftime lead against their AFC East rivals, but couldn’t sustain the momentum in the second half and let New England storm back for a 24-19 win. This year is about the growth and development of the team, not necessarily about the wins and losses – but wins sure feel much better than losses. In Week 9, the Dolphins host the Detroit Lions, a 5-2 team that is looking to return to the playoffs in 2026 after missing out last year. A physical team that gets after their opponents each and every week, Detroit serves as an example of the success a philosophy change and roster rebuild can bring. The Lions are five years ahead of Miami on the rebuild path. The FanDuel Sportsbook oddsmakers , expect Detroit to use that advantage to come away with the win on Sunday. Dolphins fan confidence Despite the losses mounting, Dolphins fans seem to see the course laid out by general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley. They have the players believing in them, and the fans seem to also trust them. Each week, we ask you to weigh in on how you are feeling about the direction of the Dolphins. This year, the fans have consistently demonstrated their trust for the new management team and in the direction of the franchise. That doesn’t mean the losses don’t affect fans’ feelings. Heading into last week, 97 percent of fans thought Miami was headed in the right direction, nearing an all-time high after the team’s win over the New York Jets. After the loss to the New England Patriots in Week 8, and as they prepare to face the Detroit Lions in Week 9, fan confidence dropped somewhat, but support for the team remains overwhelming. top.title: Meadowbrook volleyball headed back to OHSSA Final Four after regional title
top.description: CAMBRIDGE — To the untrained eye, the Meadowbrook Colts make volleyball look effortless. But behind their nearly flawless sweeps and staggering postseason run lies a simple, sweat-soaked truth: perfection is just the byproduct of the amount of hard work that is put forth. Sweeping past Frankfort Adena (25-16, 25-21, 25-16) in the OHSAA Division V regional championship game on Saturday, November 7, the Meadowbrook Colts captured their second consecutive Final Four appearance, and their third in a remarkable seven-year run of reaching the OHSAA regionals. A record-breaking postseason run With the victory, the Colts improve to 25-1 overall and have now rattled off nine consecutive set wins during their current postseason surge−adding to a dominating performance where they dropped just four sets total during the regular season. Next up for Meadowbrook is an OHSAA State Semifinal matchup against Coldwater on Friday, Nov. 13, 2026 at 11:30 a.m. at the Pam Evans Smith Arena on the campus of Wittenberg University in Springfield, Ohio. Trusting the process While the Colts' play on the volleyball court can make their success look routine, veteran senior Kara Lauder knows the blueprint behind reaching that success. "Our success really comes down to repetition on from a lot of hard work, and being both mentally and physically ready to perform," Launder explained following Thursday's Division V regional semifinal victory over Martins Ferry. "We rep it every single day in practice, so when we get to the game it all just seems to come together for us." Balanced attack fuels success That hard work translates directly into a balanced stat sheet with plenty of contributions from a variety of players. "Sophomore Addie Schultice powered the Colts' attack with 11 kills, 12 points, and 14 digs. Freshman setter Bricelynn Vargeson handed out 41 assists along with 13 digs and two points. Senior Natalee Norman contributed 13 points, 12 kills, and 16 digs, while senior Lyla Thompson chipped in with eight kills, 11 points and three blocks. Junior Presleigh Valentine finished with eight kills, nine points and a pair of digs. Eyes on history For head coach Kelly Zehnder, returning to the state's biggest stage is the validation of a culture built over years of sustained success. "We feel good to get back where we want to be−the Final Four with an opportunity to make school history by doing something that's not been done yet," Zehnder said. "That opportunity before us is great, and our girls deserve it with their hard work and dedication." Looking forward to the challenges awaiting them during next weekend's Final Four, Zehnder emphasized her team's competitive hunger. "Certainly every year feels good, and we are proud of what we have done this season," Zehnder added. "But we know we are going to face some really good competition when we get to the Dayton-Springfield area next weekend. But we are looking forward to being tested by some of the best volleyball teams in the state.

top.title: 'That's Reece' - World Cup semi-final brings out best and worst of Walsh
top.description: On a fractious night in Sydney, it was no surprise to see Reece Walsh at the centre of the action – for better or worse. The full-back scored three of Australia's eight tries as they beat Samoa 44-12 to reach a 16th successive men's Rugby League World Cup final. His two second-half tries helped keep a burgeoning Samoa comeback at bay, while his first-half effort demonstrated his skill and showmanship. On 32 minutes, Walsh administered the harshest of punishments on Samoa for the smallest amount of defensive laxity, racing through the tiniest gap on the left to score. In front of approximately 40,000 spectators, the Kangaroos' number one celebrated with a backflip. It was the kind of celebration you expect from a man once christened by Australian Rugby League Commission chairman Peter V'landys as "the Justin Bieber of rugby league" and "charisma on steroids". But while thrilling the fans, it gives kittens to those in charge. Walsh lost his boot during the flip; when sitting down to put it back on, TV commentators fretted he had injured himself. Australia coach Kevin Walters pointedly said there would be no backflips in the second half during a half-time interview – and indeed Walsh reined himself in. "That's just Reece," Walters told the post-match media conference. "He always brings up something you don't expect. "The backflip was no different. Impressive though. He did it for some sick kids. They all asked him to do a backflip if he scored a try, so you can't really be against that when he's putting a smile on kids' faces." 'Catching the high ball is difficult' Walsh has scored five tries in three matches at this tournament [Getty Images] More concerning for Walters will be the mistakes Walsh made as he got swept up in the feverish atmosphere. Two minutes before Walsh's first try, Samoa's Stephen Crichton appeared to have grounded to close the score to 16-6 after Francis Manuleleua had beaten the Aussie full-back to a high ball. A slow-motion replay led to the debatable conclusion Manuleleua had knocked on. Whether the correct call or not, it was a massive let-off for Walsh. Samoa began to lose their heads soon after, with a major flashpoint coming after Walsh was ruled to have been dangerously tackled. It was Walsh himself who instigated the ruck after the incident. Walsh quickly responded after both Samoan scores, keeping them at arm's length while scoring his first international hat-trick. He needed to after the first one, as Crichton did get his try in the second half after Walsh dropped a bomb. Magic and mistakes go hand in hand, which is the risk Walters has taken by preferring Walsh at full-back to James Tedesco - who was player of the match as he helped Sydney Roosters win last month's NRL Grand Final. It was the team’s second straight loss and third of the season, and it likely ended any hope of a College Football Playoff run. Not surprisingly, plenty of former Buckeyes were furious about what they saw. Several former Ohio State players took to social media during and after the game to rip the team’s performance, with some even calling for major changes in Columbus. top.title: 2. Bundesliga: Heidenheim and Hannover share the points in four-goal thriller
top.description: 2. Bundesliga: Heidenheim and Hannover share the points in four-goal thriller The visitors made the brighter start and came close to opening the scoring inside the opening 15 minutes. Benjamin Källman did well to get in behind the Heidenheim defence before pulling the ball back for Husseyn Chakroun, who somehow missed the target with the goal at his mercy. Hannover continued to look dangerous, with Marcel Hartel and Stefán Teitur Thórdarson also threatening, while Heidenheim struggled to create much of note in the opening stages. Despite the visitors looking the more likely to score, it was Frank Schmidt’s side who broke the deadlock shortly before half-time. A long-range free-kick from Paul Hennrich caused problems inside the Hannover penalty area, with Jean Hugonet inadvertently diverting the ball into the path of Tim Siersleben, who reacted quickest to head home from close range in the 43rd minute. Heidenheim therefore went into the interval with a somewhat fortunate 1-0 advantage, despite Hannover having created the better opportunities during the opening 45 minutes. Sandro Wagner’s side came out with renewed purpose after the restart and were rewarded for their efforts in the 55th minute. Källman picked out Thórdarson on the edge of the penalty area, with the midfielder producing a precise first-time finish into the bottom-right corner to bring Hannover level. The visitors continued to build momentum and completed the turnaround just eight minutes later. Marcel Hartel delivered a dangerous corner into the penalty area, where Hugonet rose highest to power a header beyond Thomas Dähne and put Hannover 2-1 ahead in the 63rd minute. However, their advantage lasted less than three minutes. Heidenheim responded through a corner of their own, with substitute Christian Conteh delivering an inviting ball towards the near post for Budu Zivzivadze to glance a header into the net and restore parity at 2-2. Both sides subsequently pushed for a winner in an increasingly open encounter. Hannover continued to threaten through Chakroun, while Heidenheim looked to take advantage of their attacking momentum following the equaliser. Neither side could find a decisive breakthrough during the closing stages, however, with the points ultimately shared after an entertaining afternoon in Heidenheim. The result extends Heidenheim’s winless run, while Hannover will take encouragement from their second-half response after coming from behind to take the lead, even if they were unable to hold on for all three points.

top.title: Messi Makes History, Back-to-Back MLS Golden Boot Wins
top.description: Nov 7, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; a fan holds up a Inter Miami CF forward Lionel Messi (10) sign during a game against Charlotte FC at Nu Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Lionel Messi has become the first player in Major League Soccer history to win back-to-back Golden Boot awards . The Inter Miami forward finished the 2026 regular season with a league-high 26 goals, according to ESPN . This feat separates him from every other striker in the league’s short history. At 39 years old, Messi is not just scoring; he is dominating the statistical landscape while others struggle to keep pace. The numbers tell the whole story without any need for hype. Messi recorded 26 goals in 31 appearances (29 starts). He also added 17 assists, giving him a total of 43 goal contributions for the season. This massive output came despite a disappointing 3-3 draw with Charlotte FC in his final regular-season game on Saturday. Miami surrendered a three-goal lead in that match, but the result did not change Messi’s standing. He finished four clear of his nearest rival, FC Dallas forward Petar Musa. Respect Earned Through Work Talent gets you on the field, but consistency keeps you there. Messi has now been the top scorer in multiple MLS regular seasons, a feat only six players have ever achieved. His coach, Cristian “Kily” González, sees the effort behind the stats. González also noted that “None of them can compare to him when it comes to respect for his colleagues.” This respect is not just talk. In 2025, Messi secured the Golden Boot by netting 29 goals across only 28 matches. He followed that up with 26 goals this year. Inter Miami advanced to second place in the Eastern Conference thanks to his efforts. The team clinched a playoff spot and secured a ticket to the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup, their fourth straight time. Messi is now the front-runner to win the league MVP award again, having already won it in 2024 and 2025. Rivalry Records and Playoff Stakes While Messi claimed the individual title, the team battle saw a different outcome. Following a 2-0 Saturday victory over FC Cincinnati, Nashville SC established a new MLS single-season points record of 77. “It’s a massive achievement for the club, for us as players, and yeah, it’s going to go down in history, and I think that was the message before the game,” Surridge said. Nashville also set records for most wins and fewest losses. Inter Miami finished with 60 points, well behind Nashville’s total but enough for the second seed. The seventh-seeded Columbus Crew will face Miami in a best-of-three first-round playoff series where Miami holds home-field advantage.

nigeria.title: UK lists 4 conditions migrants must meet to qualify for permanent residency
nigeria.description: The United Kingdom, UK has introduced four mandatory conditions migrants must satisfy to qualify for permanent residency under its proposed earned settlement model, which will make obtaining indefinite leave to remain (ILR) dependent on applicants’ contributions and conduct. Under the proposed reforms, migrants will no longer qualify for permanent residency almost automatically after five years in the country. Instead, the time required to secure settled status will depend on their earnings, contribution to society and immigration history. The four non-negotiable conditions, which will apply to all applicants regardless of when they arrived in the UK, include: 1. Clean criminal record: Migrants must have a spotless criminal record, with the government proposing stricter requirements than the current rules, which allow some applicants with suspended sentences of up to 12 months to qualify. 2. High English proficiency: Applicants must demonstrate a high standard of spoken English, equivalent to A-Level English as a foreign language. 3. No outstanding government debts: Migrants must have cleared any debts owed to the UK government or taxpayer before qualifying for permanent residency. 4. Sustained National Insurance contributions: Applicants must provide evidence of sustained National Insurance contributions as proof of their economic contribution to the country. Beyond these four mandatory requirements, the proposed model introduces different settlement timelines based on migrants’ earnings and contributions. Under the arrangement, the highest earners could qualify for permanent residency after three years, while migrants earning more than £50,271 annually could become eligible after five years. Certain public service workers, including doctors, nurses and teachers, would also qualify for settlement after five years. Other migrants would be subject to a new standard settlement period of 10 years, while those who have breached immigration rules would have to wait at least 20 years before qualifying. The government said the reforms recognise settled status as a significant privilege, granting migrants unrestricted access to the labour market, the National Health Service (NHS) and the welfare system. The proposed changes are intended to make permanent residency a status migrants must earn rather than an entitlement granted after a fixed period. nigeria.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Armed men suspected to be bandits have killed 12 members of the same family and abducted several residents during an attack on Gidan Taba village in Maradun Local Government Area of Zamfara State. The attack reportedly occurred on Saturday night in Dosara Birnin Kaya Ward, with the assailants setting a room ablaze after the family members reportedly locked themselves inside to avoid being abducted. A source in the area told Vanguard that the victims belonged to the family of one Mallam Muhammadu Sani, who had gathered his relatives in a single room in an attempt to protect them from the attackers. According to the source, the bandits ordered the occupants to open the door but, after they refused, set fire around the room, killing all 12 family members. Several other residents were also reportedly abducted during the raid, although the exact number of those kidnapped could not be immediately ascertained. The 12 victims were buried on Sunday morning in accordance with Islamic rites. The attack comes amid recurring bandit attacks and security concerns along the busy Gusau-Sokoto road, where commuters have continued to face threats from armed criminals. Residents condemned the killings, describing the incident as barbaric, and called on security agencies and the Zamfara State Government to intensify efforts to protect lives and property. nigeria.title: Court awards N50m damages against Pararan over defamation
nigeria.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi EFFURUN — A Delta State High Court sitting in Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area, has awarded N50 million in damages against the proprietor of Pararan Mock News, Diamond Dietanuru Osakorigho, popularly known as Pararan, over a Facebook publication found to be defamatory against Apostle Michael Akpor. The court, presided over by Justice R.D. Harriman, also ordered Osakorigho to publish an unreserved apology to the cleric in Vanguard and The Nation newspapers within 14 days. It directed that the apology must enjoy the same prominence and circulation as the original publication. The judgment was delivered on November 6, 2026, in Suit No. EHC/91/2023. The court further restrained the defendant, his agents, privies, servants and all persons acting through him from publishing or causing to be published any further defamatory, injurious or libellous statements, videos or other materials against Akpor. It also awarded N1 million as costs of the suit. The case arose from a Facebook publication made on July 20, 2022, with the caption, “Warri Pastor Kpuf 2Keke passenger”, which the court found to be false and defamatory. Reacting to the judgment, counsel to the cleric, Austin Nyekigbe, a human rights activist, described the ruling as a significant statement on responsible social media engagement. He said the judgment reinforced the principle that freedom to use social media did not confer the right to publish false and defamatory information about others. “People must learn to verify information before rushing to publish it, particularly on social media. An injustice to one is an injustice to all,” he said. Also commenting on the judgment, a Warri-based lawyer, Mrs Eloho Avwaruroro-Okoye, who was present in court, said the decision underscored the legal consequences of irresponsible online publications. According to her, freedom of expression comes with responsibility, adding that those who publish false and damaging information must be prepared to face the legal consequences. She congratulated Akpor on his victory and commended Nyekigbe for his diligence in handling the case. The legal dispute followed allegations linking Akpor and two policemen attached to him to the July 12, 2022, killing of two persons at Ugbolokposo community in Effurun. However, Nyekigbe said police investigations subsequently exonerated his client and the two officers, identified as ASP Mesoro Victor and Inspector Ignatius Achazie. He said findings from the investigation, including witness statements, vehicle identification exercises and church CCTV footage, contradicted allegations linking the cleric to the killings. According to him, the police investigation report established that Akpor was at his church when the incident occurred, concluding that he was “going on with his religious business in the Church”. nigeria.title: Troops neutralise suspected criminal, arrest five in Plateau
nigeria.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS – Troops of Operation Enduring Peace (OPEP) have neutralised a suspected notorious criminal in Wase Local Government Area and arrested five suspected phone snatchers during a raid on a hotel in Jos North Local Government Area of Plateau State. The operations also led to the recovery of 26 mobile phones and other items suspected to be stolen, including laptops, earpods and power banks. Military sources disclosed that the suspected criminal, identified as Abubakar Ango, was arrested on November 4 by troops of Sector 2 OPEP at Kukawa village in Wase. “At about 7:20 a.m. on November 6, during interrogation, the suspect reportedly confessed to involvement in several criminal activities and agreed to lead troops to his gang’s hideouts in a village forest,” the sources said. They explained that the mission was intended to facilitate the recovery of weapons and possible arrest of other members of the gang. “However, while being escorted to the location, the suspect allegedly attempted to seize the rifle of one of the soldiers, prompting an immediate response that resulted in his neutralisation,” they said. They disclosed that the five suspects were found in possession of the tracked phone, while a further search led to the recovery of 26 mobile phones, 27 pouches, three MP devices, two earpods, an HP laptop, a knife and four power banks. “The vehicle belonging to the suspects was also towed to the headquarters of Sector 1 for a comprehensive search,” the sources added. “The suspects and recovered exhibits have been taken into custody for further investigation and necessary action,” the sources said. nigeria.title: Man returns home after 28-yr journey walking around the world
nigeria.description: A British adventurer, Karl Bushby, has returned to his childhood home in Hull, northern England, after completing a 28-year walking journey around the world that covered approximately 50,000 kilometres. Bushby, 57, was welcomed by his mother, Angela, outside her terraced house on Monday, November 2, 2026, beneath a banner reading “Welcome Home Son”. Hundreds of supporters had gathered in the city centre to celebrate his return before he completed the final stretch of his journey to his mother’s home. “Sorry to keep you waiting,” he joked to the cheering crowd. “Is that it, is it done?” Bushby began the expedition, known as the Goliath Expedition, in November 1998 in Punta Arenas, southern Chile. His goal was to travel around the world and return to his hometown without using any form of motorised transport to advance his journey. Carrying a tent, a few hundred dollars and a plastic camera, he initially expected the expedition to take about 12 years. His route took him north through the Americas before crossing the frozen Bering Strait from Alaska into Russia. He subsequently travelled through Mongolia and China, swam across the Caspian Sea and continued towards Europe. The journey also involved navigating the dense Darien Gap jungle between Colombia and Panama, crossing international borders and dealing with visa restrictions. Bushby was detained after entering Russia, while funding difficulties and the global financial crisis of 2008, which cost him major sponsors, contributed to delays that extended the expedition to 28 years. In the final stages of the journey, he swam across the English Channel last month, clearing one of the remaining major obstacles before walking the final distance to Hull. Speaking after his arrival, Bushby acknowledged the support he received from people and organisations across different countries. “They say it takes a village, but literally it took a world to get me here,” he said. “The kindness of strangers, so many, from individuals to nation-states, to get me back here today. I didn’t do this alone. There was a big team. The biggest team. Earth.” A feature-length documentary about his expedition is currently in production, while Bushby is expected to begin a speaking tour across England in the coming weeks. FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Zuffa LLC) The fans want a Justin Gaethje vs. Ilia Topuria rematch. Ilia Topuria wants it. The UFC wants it. But Justin Gaethje does not, according to his manager Ali Abdelaziz. Gaethje took the UFC lightweight title off Topuria in a brutal war on the White House lawn back in June, forcing Topuria’s corner to throw in the towel after the fourth round. Few had given Justin a chance of winning, and now “The Highlight” seems uninterested in giving Ilia a chance to win that fight back. Topuria just did a media blitz of interviews, and a big topic of discussion was a potential Gaethje rematch. Topuria put up a poll on social media to ask his fans who they’d rather see him face off against. After 24 hours, Justin Gaethje edged out Paddy Pimblett, 474,000 votes to 385,000. Alas, there continues to be no interest in the fight from Gaethje’s side. 🚨‼️Ali Abdelaziz completely shuts down the possibility of an Ilia Topuria rematch 👀 🗣️“This rematch will never happen, and I agree with him. The Bulldogs rolled past their SEC rivals in Oxford and put themselves back in the hunt for the number one spot. This win comes right after No. 1 Miami lost to Notre Dame, clearing the path for Georgia to climb back to the top of the US LBM Coaches Poll. Georgia’s defense held star quarterback Trinidad Chambliss to just 170 passing yards with no touchdowns and one interception. The Buckeyes now have two straight defeats, and their chances for the College Football Playoff look like they are toast. Per Yahoo Sports, the AP voters will drop Ohio State in the rankings after the Buckeyes were handled at home by Oregon. This follows a previous loss to USC, leaving Ryan Day’s team with a shaky resume despite wins against Iowa and Indiana. The collapse of Ohio State highlights how fast things can change in college football. Teams that look strong in September can crater by November if they lose key games. The Buckeyes are now in a spot where they need to win out just to stay relevant. Meanwhile, Georgia used their own loss to Auburn as a reset to become the most complete team in the country. They have turned back into a dominant force when it matters most. The New Order at the Top With Miami’s loss and Georgia’s win, the top of the polls is set for a major shakeup. Following their Holy War victory over BYU, Utah holds a perfect 9-0 record, marking the first top-10 clash in the series history. The Utes are now one of the last two unbeaten teams left in the nation and are locked in for the Big 12 title game. Per Yahoo Sports, Utah could rise to No. 2 in the coaches poll while UCLA moves to No. 3 after staying perfect. Notre Dame also secured its spot in the playoff chase by beating Miami 31-24 in South Bend. By executing a critical red zone stop with less than four minutes remaining, the Fighting Irish prevented a devastating defeat. They now look forward to Boston College, SMU, and Syracuse to end the year.

Trusting the process While the Colts' play on the volleyball court can make their success look routine, veteran senior Kara Lauder knows the blueprint behind reaching that success. "Our success really comes down to repetition on from a lot of hard work, and being both mentally and physically ready to perform," Launder explained following Thursday's Division V regional semifinal victory over Martins Ferry. "We rep it every single day in practice, so when we get to the game it all just seems to come together for us." In front of approximately 40,000 spectators, the Kangaroos' number one celebrated with a backflip. It was the kind of celebration you expect from a man once christened by Australian Rugby League Commission chairman Peter V'landys as "the Justin Bieber of rugby league" and "charisma on steroids". But while thrilling the fans, it gives kittens to those in charge. Walsh lost his boot during the flip; when sitting down to put it back on, TV commentators fretted he had injured himself. Australia coach Kevin Walters pointedly said there would be no backflips in the second half during a half-time interview – and indeed Walsh reined himself in. "That's just Reece," Walters told the post-match media conference. "He always brings up something you don't expect. "The backflip was no different. Impressive though. He did it for some sick kids. sports.description: 2. Bundesliga: Heidenheim and Hannover share the points in four-goal thriller The visitors made the brighter start and came close to opening the scoring inside the opening 15 minutes. Benjamin Källman did well to get in behind the Heidenheim defence before pulling the ball back for Husseyn Chakroun, who somehow missed the target with the goal at his mercy. Hannover continued to look dangerous, with Marcel Hartel and Stefán Teitur Thórdarson also threatening, while Heidenheim struggled to create much of note in the opening stages. Despite the visitors looking the more likely to score, it was Frank Schmidt’s side who broke the deadlock shortly before half-time. A long-range free-kick from Paul Hennrich caused problems inside the Hannover penalty area, with Jean Hugonet inadvertently diverting the ball into the path of Tim Siersleben, who reacted quickest to head home from close range in the 43rd minute. Heidenheim therefore went into the interval with a somewhat fortunate 1-0 advantage, despite Hannover having created the better opportunities during the opening 45 minutes. Sandro Wagner’s side came out with renewed purpose after the restart and were rewarded for their efforts in the 55th minute. Källman picked out Thórdarson on the edge of the penalty area, with the midfielder producing a precise first-time finish into the bottom-right corner to bring Hannover level. The visitors continued to build momentum and completed the turnaround just eight minutes later. Marcel Hartel delivered a dangerous corner into the penalty area, where Hugonet rose highest to power a header beyond Thomas Dähne and put Hannover 2-1 ahead in the 63rd minute. However, their advantage lasted less than three minutes. Heidenheim responded through a corner of their own, with substitute Christian Conteh delivering an inviting ball towards the near post for Budu Zivzivadze to glance a header into the net and restore parity at 2-2. Both sides subsequently pushed for a winner in an increasingly open encounter. Hannover continued to threaten through Chakroun, while Heidenheim looked to take advantage of their attacking momentum following the equaliser. Neither side could find a decisive breakthrough during the closing stages, however, with the points ultimately shared after an entertaining afternoon in Heidenheim. The result extends Heidenheim’s winless run, while Hannover will take encouragement from their second-half response after coming from behind to take the lead, even if they were unable to hold on for all three points.

sports.title: Messi Makes History, Back-to-Back MLS Golden Boot Wins
sports.description: Nov 7, 2026; Miami, Florida, USA; a fan holds up a Inter Miami CF forward Lionel Messi (10) sign during a game against Charlotte FC at Nu Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Lionel Messi has become the first player in Major League Soccer history to win back-to-back Golden Boot awards . The Inter Miami forward finished the 2026 regular season with a league-high 26 goals, according to ESPN . This feat separates him from every other striker in the league’s short history. At 39 years old, Messi is not just scoring; he is dominating the statistical landscape while others struggle to keep pace. The numbers tell the whole story without any need for hype. Messi recorded 26 goals in 31 appearances (29 starts). He also added 17 assists, giving him a total of 43 goal contributions for the season. This massive output came despite a disappointing 3-3 draw with Charlotte FC in his final regular-season game on Saturday. Miami surrendered a three-goal lead in that match, but the result did not change Messi’s standing. He finished four clear of his nearest rival, FC Dallas forward Petar Musa. Respect Earned Through Work Talent gets you on the field, but consistency keeps you there. Messi has now been the top scorer in multiple MLS regular seasons, a feat only six players have ever achieved. His coach, Cristian “Kily” González, sees the effort behind the stats. González also noted that “None of them can compare to him when it comes to respect for his colleagues.” This respect is not just talk. In 2025, Messi secured the Golden Boot by netting 29 goals across only 28 matches. He followed that up with 26 goals this year. Inter Miami advanced to second place in the Eastern Conference thanks to his efforts. The team clinched a playoff spot and secured a ticket to the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup, their fourth straight time. Messi is now the front-runner to win the league MVP award again, having already won it in 2024 and 2025. Rivalry Records and Playoff Stakes While Messi claimed the individual title, the team battle saw a different outcome. Following a 2-0 Saturday victory over FC Cincinnati, Nashville SC established a new MLS single-season points record of 77. “It’s a massive achievement for the club, for us as players, and yeah, it’s going to go down in history, and I think that was the message before the game,” Surridge said. Nashville also set records for most wins and fewest losses. Inter Miami finished with 60 points, well behind Nashville’s total but enough for the second seed. The seventh-seeded Columbus Crew will face Miami in a best-of-three first-round playoff series where Miami holds home-field advantage.

technology.title: Physicists listened to electrical noise to crack a superconductor mystery
technology.description: Superconductors carry electricity without resistance, but most only work a few degrees above absolute zero. In the late 1980s, copper-based materials called cuprates were found to superconduct at higher temperatures—reachable with affordable liquid nitrogen. Yet nearly 40 years later, physicists still don't agree on why. In a recent Science study, a team of physicists led by Milan Allan of Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich and Ingmar Swart of Utrecht University in the Netherlands has found some answers by listening to the faint electrical crackle of current flowing into a cuprate. The missing electrons Central to the mystery of cuprates’ high-temperature superconductivity is a strange state called the pseudogap. “The pseudogap is a phenomenon of missing electrons,” Allan said. Above the temperature at which cuprates become superconducting, some of their electrons seem to vanish—measurements find far fewer of them at the energies where they should be. “Everybody knows that from different probes, you see that there's these vanishing electrons, but nobody knows why,” Allan said. technology.title: Doom delivers five minutes of terminal violence on an IBM mainframe
technology.description: Can an IBM Z mainframe run Doom? Of course it can. The more interesting question is whether you can play it through a text terminal without ruining your eyesight. WND Software's browser demo connects to an IBM Z mainframe over SSH using its terminal emulator. Wojciech Graj's DOOM-ASCII supplies the text-based carnage, replacing conventional graphics with colored characters. There's no sound. It is, however, completely playable (although you might need to recalibrate your vision to work out what is going on, particularly with regard to distant objects). Sessions are limited to five minutes, with room for up to 50 simultaneous users, but we had no trouble getting in. ASCII also presented no issues once the game was in motion. This writer played the original shareware release on an Amstrad ALT386SX portable, so squinting at an indistinct demon felt reassuringly familiar. That Doom can be persuaded to run on an IBM Z mainframe is not particularly noteworthy. The code has turned up everywhere from databases to PCB designers . Even the humble Pi Pico was roped into the fun. Keeping the action playable through a text terminal is the more entertaining achievement. A year ago, an IBM consultant persuaded Doom to run on IBM Z and LinuxONE using VNC to bring the pixelated mayhem to life. Using a terminal emulator, while a neat demonstration of the capabilities of WND's software, is perhaps more an example of "because I can" masochism. It's undeniably an enjoyable way to burn through five minutes. No installation or login required – just a willingness to shoot at punctuation. ®

technology.title: Internet governance about to get its quadrennial stress test at ITU meeting
technology.description: The International Telecommunications Union (ITU) kicks off its quadrennial plenipotentiary on Monday, and internet governance organizations are bracing in case the event becomes a forum for nation-states to try to challenge their roles. The ITU is the United Nations' specialized agency for information and communication technologies, meaning its members are nation-states. The body's role is to facilitate international connectivity, which it does by managing radio spectrum, satellite orbits, and working on relevant technical standards. Its key standards are pervasive. ITU-T X.509 sets out the rules of public key infrastructure. ITU-T E.164 governs telephone numbers. ITU-T H.264 and 265 define the video codecs used for most online streams. The ITU's role is largely uncontested, yet its work gets very close to that of the organizations who work on technologies that make the internet work. Those bodies include the Internet Engineering Task Force (IETF); the Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN), which oversees the domain name system; and the regional internet registries (RIRs), which manage IP addresses. The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) works on HTML, CSS, and accessibility. Governments participate in work at those internet governance bodies but are just one voice among many and can't override the consensus-driven decision-making process they use, under a system which has come to be known as the multi-stakeholder governance model. At a 2025 event called WSIS+20, the United Nations endorsed multi-stakeholder governance by deciding that its Internet Governance Forum (IGF) should become a permanent body. That decision effectively endorsed multi-stakeholder governance, and kept the ITU out of internet standards. Yet the IGF hasn't met since WSIS+20, so it is yet to start operating meaningfully as a permanent body. This year's ITU meeting is therefore a moment at which stakeholders can stress-test the delicate balance between the ITU, internet governance bodies, and the emerging IGF. Such a test could see ITU members try to have it pursue new fields that overlap with work performed by internet governance organizations. This has already happened before. China tried to have the ITU work on " New IP" – a major revision to internet protocol, a technology the IETF manages. In 2022, Russia and China backed a candidate for the ITU presidency who favored giving nations a stronger role in internet governance, potentialy by having the ITU take over some standards work. That candidate was not elected. Ahead of next week's meetings, the Internet Society published a background paper that declared it is "actively challenging proposals that could affect the Internet's underlying technical architecture or increase fragmentation, as well as those that could affect connectivity, particularly for remote, underserved, and unserved communities." science.title: Scientists simulate an Earth without life to help hunt for aliens and inhabited worlds
science.description: A new computer simulation that depicts Earth, or a rocky planet in general, without life is the latest tool in the quest to discover whether or not we are alone in the universe. Life leaves its mark on a planet, particularly its atmosphere, in the form of a mixture of biochemically created gases. Some are obvious, while others can be produced by both biology and geology, meaning that distinguishing a planet that has life from one that does not, solely based on what gases we can detect in its atmosphere, can be difficult. The key is in knowing which atmospheric conditions can be explained without life. To aid in distinguishing between habitable and inhabited planets, planetary scientist Samantha Gilbert-Janizek of the University of California, Riverside, developed a model that simulates the evolution of a rocky planet without life. "The model can help us see how habitable but non-living planets might mimic living planets," Gilbert-Janizek, who was a PhD student at the University of Washington when the research was conducted, said in a statement. Gilbert-Janizek built upon a model previously developed by Washington’s Rory Barnes that simulated the core, mantle, and crust of a planet. This new model pushed the simulation two steps further by incorporating the surface and atmosphere of the planet as well. In all, the model simulates 19 properties of a rocky planet that are not related to life, including the amount of heat a planet receives from its star , the exchange of heat and chemicals from the core to the surface, and the outflow of certain gases from the subsurface. Gilbert-Janizek’s starting point was to simulate the development of Earth had life never arisen here, therefore providing a baseline with which to compare to exoplanets . She ran the simulation from the birth of Earth 4.5 billion years ago to 500 million years into the future. The result was a lifeless world, but one that still had oceans and an atmosphere. "When we interpret observations of an exoplanet’s atmosphere, this tool will help us determine the probability that what we observe indicates life on the surface," said Gilbert-Janizek. An illustration shows the landscape of a primordial Earth before life arose as lightning splits the skies (Image credit: Robert Lea (created with Canva)) What makes the simulation especially useful is its plug-and-play nature. Researchers can simply apply the bulk properties of whichever planet they are studying to the model, and then just let it run. If the result is a planet with an atmosphere that matches what is detected spectroscopically by the James Webb Space Telescope or, in the future, the various extremely large 30-meter-plus ground-based telescopes or NASA’s planned Habitable Worlds Observatory , then we know that planet probably does not have life as we know it. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. Ingenuity was only designed to make five flights, but made it to 72 until its blades were damaged during a landing on Jan. 18, 2024. NASA is now planning a SkyFall mission on Mars that would use three helicopters, and which may launch as soon as late 2028 for the Red Planet. Dragonfly, however, is not the first mission to Titan: that would be Huygens , which operated for just a few hours on Jan. 14, 2005 after deploying from the Cassini spacecraft. Huygens was the first lander on an outer solar system world, and measured Titan's atmosphere and took data from the surface. A mosaic image of Saturn's moon Titan composed of images produced by the Cassini spacecraft. (Image credit: NASA/JPL/University of Arizona/University of Idaho) For its part, Cassini flew by Titan more than 100 times before the mission concluded in September 2017 , providing valuable long-term data about the moon from above. Dragonfly aims to show the moon from up close for about 3.3 Earth years. Its destinations will include dunes and a young impact crater called Selk, according to NASA. "Dragonfly is expected to make one flight every one to two Titan days, which is called a Tsol and lasts about 16 Earth days," NASA officials added of the mission . Dragonfly will stop at a variety of geologic sites, where it will collect samples of surface material for analysis inside the rotorcraft by a suite of scientific instruments." science.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
science.description: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Star Wars Zero Company and Galactic Racer 's restrained scope and confidence have been infectious, and, as it turns out, they're already recognized by all the parties involved as double-A success stories . The original Burnout studio, Criterion, would have been an excellent candidate, but instead they were sent to work in the Battlefield mines. Still, someone was interested in the idea, and the end result is glorious. science.title: 'I think we will prevail': NASA chief Jared Isaacman on Artemis, China and the new moon race (exclusive)
science.description: null NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman is serious about launching "big rockets" to the moon every single year for the agency's Artemis program. And the new space race with China is fueling that ambition. "I feel good. I feel like we are certainly on a more achievable path to the lunar surface today than where we were before," Isaacman told Space.com. We recently sat down with the NASA chief to discuss the state of the Artemis program , and, off the bat, he made it clear that he's confident in the U.S. space program following the success of April's Artemis II mission around the moon. In fact, just prior to our conversation, it was announced that Artemis II commander Reid Wiseman will become the new deputy director of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory. But the road from Artemis II's success to crewed lunar landings and, later, a permanent moon base will take a lot of launches of NASA's Space Launch System (SLS) megarocket, Isaacman stressed. "You know, a lot of people, especially in the space community, start getting [into] if the landers are there or not. I don't really care about that right now. What I care about is that we are launching big rockets no less than once a year," he said. "I think that's imperative for NASA to be doing these deep-space human spaceflight missions right now," Isaacman added. "So, we had a great mission in April of '26. We will launch again in '27." That coming launch will be for Artemis III, a crewed mission to low Earth orbit that will test docking procedures between NASA's Orion capsule and one or both of the Artemis program's private lunar landers — SpaceX's Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon. "We need to continue to exercise those muscles," he said, referring to SLS liftoffs. "And, honestly, once a year isn't great, either. science.description: null SpaceX just launched a classified mission for the U.S. military. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base this evening (Nov. 6) at 7:48 p.m. EST (4:48 p.m. local California time; 0048 GMT on Nov. 7), rising into the sky as the sun sank toward the Pacific. The launch kicked off the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force , which we know little about. Neither SpaceX nor the Space Force told us much about USSF-432 beforehand, and we learned tonight; SpaceX cut its webcast off about 10 minutes into the flight, shortly after the Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth for a landing. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base on Nov. 6, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) That touchdown occurred aboard the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed downrange in the Pacific Ocean. It wrapped up the eighth flight for this particular booster, which is designated 1095. The Falcon 9's upper stage, meanwhile, continued carrying its mystery payload skyward. It could be headed to low Earth orbit , outside observers speculate. "It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites for the USSF's Space Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio based on SpaceX's Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches," NextSpaceflight.com wrote in a mission description . Starlink is SpaceX's LEO broadband megaconstellation, which consists of more than 11,000 active satellites. Starshield is a similar system designed to provide services to the U.S. military and its allies. Starshield satellites are believed to be based heavily on the Starlink spacecraft bus. The vast majority of Falcon 9 missions in 2026 — more than 70% — have been devoted to building out the Starlink megaconstellation. SpaceX has also launched six other missions this year. Three were operational flights of the company's Falcon Heavy rocket, while the other three were test missions of its next-gen Starship vehicle. SpaceX plans to retire both the Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy shortly after the fully reusable Starship, the biggest and most powerful rocket ever built, is up and running.

science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so.
